> # Rio Tinto BioIron pause and ZESTY investment - ABC News verification notes

>
> ## Verified source notes
>
> ABC independently reported that Rio Tinto stopped the previously announced
> A$215 million BioIron research-centre and pilot plan and redirected the
> Rockingham site toward the Calix ZESTY demonstration project. Rio Tinto said
> that BioIron furnace designs needed further development to reduce technical
> risk and improve performance, while retaining a longer-term R&D interest.
>
> ABC reported Rio Tinto support of more than A$35 million for ZESTY and noted
> that the project already had nearly A$45 million of ARENA grant support. The
> report described detailed engineering before a final investment decision in
> 2026; it did not report that FID, construction, commissioning, or commercial
> operation had been achieved.
>
> Calix chief executive Phil Hodgson told ABC that grid electricity may be used
> during demonstration testing, so not every tonne produced at the Kwinana
> demonstration would necessarily be zero-emissions. He distinguished the
> purpose of the demonstration from a future commercial unit designed to use
> zero-emission energy.
>
> Curtin University associate professor Tejas Bhatelia described BioIron and
> ZESTY as complementary rather than directly interchangeable routes and warned
> that a Pilbara green-iron industry would need additional renewable-energy,
> water, and workforce infrastructure.
>
> ## Cross-check conclusion
>
> The independent report corroborates the official BioIron pause, the ZESTY
> funding pivot, and the pre-FID engineering stage. It also supplies an important
> boundary missing from promotional summaries: demonstration output cannot be
> labelled uniformly zero-emission unless the actual electricity and hydrogen
> supply are verified.
